newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's may downgrade Mitsui Fudosan debt.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may downgrade Mitsui Fudosan debt.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Wednesday that it had placed its A2 rating for the senior unsecured long-term debt securities of Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd under review for possible downgrade.

Moody's said it had also placed its A2 ratings for Mitsui subsidiary Mitsui Fudosan International Capital Inc's global medium-term note programme and Mitsui's Japanese domestic shelf registration under review for possible downgrade. Mitsui's prime-1 short-term rating and its subsidiary Mitsui Fudosan (New York) Inc were also placed under review for possible downgrade, it said.

Mitsui recently announced a 310 billion yen asset disposal plan to achieve its debt reduction target. The plan will include sales of the company's non-performing and non-strategic property holdings, which will accompany realisation of substantial latent losses in the properties, leading to a sizable net loss for the current fiscal year, it said.

"In the context of sustainability of Mitsui's operating performance over the intermediate term, Moody's will review the value and quality of Mitsui's asset portfolio after the planned disposal," it said. It added that it would evaluate Mitsui's ability to execute its asset-disposal plan in the midst of the continuing soft property market in Japan.
Moody's said it would also assess the positive effects of Mitsui's planned debt reduction on its coverage measures.
